item.title: Re: okay so here's the deal with my new black queen format article
item.content:encoded:
I am 100% in favor of other people making more GAW SCPs in general, including their misters. If you're worried about infringing on the general tone or direction of the series, there are a few guidelines that I would like people to follow:

  • Gamers Against Weed SCPs should not be harmful to anyone who doesn't obviously deserve it. It's fine if they can be used to hurt people, but that shouldn't be an obvious use for them.
  • Misters Against Weed should have an obvious use for kids. They don't have to be kid-oriented, but you should be able to look at one and say "okay, I can see why a kid would want this".
  • GAW's members are mostly forum trolls and various internet-dwellers who love jokes and pranks, and are willing to use anomalies to this effect. While they are exceptionally irreverent, they can also be pretty competent and very dedicated to their 'craft'.
    • That said, while they are extremely online and immersed in cyberculture, they DO generally have lives and interests beyond that, and there need not be any connection to the internet in their pieces. They lean left politically (they don't get much more centrist than Bernie Sanders), and may engage in political activity, but that's not their main purpose.
  • They don't stick their name on stuff unless that's part of the joke (as it is with the Misters Against Weed). They're not out for recognition or signaling allegiance to the group. If you want to connect them to an article that isn't a mister, you may have to establish that connection by describing traditional investigative techniques.

Beyond that, you're free to interpret Gamers Against Weed or any of the unclaimed Misters as you see fit as far as I'm concerned. If you want any help or feedback when writing one, feel free to shoot me a message.

item.title: okay so here's the deal with my new black queen format article
